entries.title: Wizard movie and pretend potions
entries.body: Tonight we watched a wizard movie on the couch and Mom made popcorn with extra butter. In the movie they made potions in a big pot with smoke coming out. I want to make potions for real. After the movie I mixed water and grape juice and a little bit of dish soap in a cup and it got bubbly. I said it was a potion for flying. Mom said it was a potion for cleaning up. I wonder if real scientists started out making potions.
entries.favorite: Mixing the purple potion in the cup
entries.highlight: Watched a wizard movie with Mom and made a bubbly pretend potion afterward, wondering if real scientists started that way.

entries.title: Ivy dropped her ice cream
entries.body: Today we went to the ice cream shop with my whole family. I got mint chip in a cone. Ivy got strawberry but she was walking and it went splat on the sidewalk. She cried really loud. So I let her have some of mine, but only from the side I did not lick yet. Dad said that was a big brother move. The ice cream melted really fast on the sidewalk and I wonder why it melts faster on the ground than in the cup.
entries.favorite: Sharing my mint chip with Ivy
entries.highlight: Shared his mint chip cone with his little sister Ivy after she dropped hers, and Dad praised him for it.

entries.title: Shopping list for the egg drop
entries.body: I need to make a parachute so an egg can fall and not crack. So me and Mom went to the store to get stuff. I made a list like a real scientist. It said eggs, string, plastic bags, tape, and cotton balls. The lady at the store asked what I was making and I said an egg parachute and she said good luck to your egg. Mom let me hold the eggs in the cart. I did not crack any yet.
entries.highlight: Made a supply list and shopped with Mom for an egg-drop parachute project.

entries.title: Jupiter with a red spot
entries.body: I drew a picture of Jupiter today. Jupiter is the biggest planet so I used the whole paper. I made stripes with orange and brown and tan crayons. Then I made the big red spot. My book says the red spot is a storm that is bigger than Earth. That is so crazy. I wonder how long that storm has been spinning. Mom hung it on the fridge with the magnet shaped like a lemon. Ivy wanted to color on it but I said no, it is finished.
entries.favorite: Mom putting it on the fridge
entries.highlight: Drew a big striped Jupiter with its Great Red Spot, and Mom hung it on the fridge.

entries.title: Thanksgiving and the planet model
entries.body: Today was Thanksgiving. We had turkey and mashed potatoes and I had two rolls. After dinner Dad got out the solar system kit we bought. We painted all the planet balls. I painted Mars red and Neptune blue. Dad did Earth because it has a lot of details. The paint has to dry all night so we cannot hang it yet. I am thankful for Dad, and for planets, and for pumpkin pie.
entries.highlight: Spent Thanksgiving evening painting a solar system model with Dad.

entries.title: Saturn's rings were the hardest
entries.body: Today me and Dad finished the solar system model and we hung it from my ceiling with clear thread. Saturn's rings were the hardest. They kept sliding down and Dad had to use hot glue, and I was not allowed to touch the hot glue. Now when I lay in bed I can see all the planets. The sun is in the middle and it is the biggest one. I said goodnight to all eight planets.
entries.favorite: Seeing the planets hanging over my bed
entries.highlight: Finished hanging the solar system model over his bed with Dad, who hot-glued Saturn's slippery rings.

entries.title: Purple slime with Nadia
entries.body: Nadia came over after school and we did experiments in the kitchen. We made purple slime with glue and the contact solution. It was too sticky at first so we put in more solution and then it got stretchy. We said we are lab partners forever and we shook hands with slime hands. Then some slime fell on the carpet. Mom was not happy. Now there is a slime spot by the couch.
entries.highlight: Made purple slime with Nadia, declared themselves lab partners forever, and left a slime spot on the carpet.

entries.title: Where did all the bugs go?
entries.body: I went in the backyard with my magnifying glass to look for bugs. But it was so cold and I could not find any. Not one. I looked in the grass and on the fence. Then Dad helped me flip over the old log and there was one roly poly under it, all curled up in a ball. I think the bugs are hiding because they do not have jackets. I wonder where they go to sleep in winter.
entries.favorite: Finding a roly poly under the log
entries.highlight: Searched for bugs in the cold backyard and found only one curled-up roly poly under a log.

entries.title: Lemons for a lemon battery
entries.body: I saw a video where you can make electricity with lemons. So me and Mom went to the store to get lemons and zinc screws and copper wire. I made a list like a real scientist and checked everything off. We got six lemons. The cashier asked if we were making lemonade and I said no, a battery. She laughed. Mom said the copper wire was at the hardware store so we had to go to two stores.
entries.highlight: Shopped at two stores with Mom for lemons, zinc screws and copper wire to build a lemon battery.

entries.title: A black hole book from the library
entries.body: It was library day today. I got a book about black holes. It has a picture of a black hole on the front and it looks like a hole in space with fire around it. A black hole is so heavy that it eats everything, even light. I wonder what happens if you fall in one. The librarian said I am a fast reader because I read three pages before we even lined up. I am going to read it to Ivy but she might get scared.
entries.highlight: Checked out a book about black holes on library day and the librarian called him a fast reader.

entries.title: Felix and the volcano that did not erupt
entries.body: Felix came over to play today. We wanted to make a volcano but we only had a little bit of baking soda. So it only fizzed a tiny bit. Felix made a face like it was a giant eruption anyway and we laughed so hard. Then we made slime but we were careful this time and did it on a tray. Mom said thank you for using the tray. Felix said next time we need a whole box of baking soda.
entries.highlight: Played with Felix, tried a small volcano that barely fizzed, and made slime carefully on a tray.

entries.title: Egg drop take two
entries.body: Today me and Mom did the egg drop off the back deck. The first try the parachute did not open and the egg cracked and it was gooey. Then we made the parachute bigger with a grocery bag and put cotton balls around the egg. The second try it floated down slow and it did not crack. I yelled it worked. I want to do it again but bigger, maybe from the roof. Mom said no roof.
entries.highlight: Did an egg-drop parachute with Mom; it failed the first time and worked on the second try with a bigger parachute.

entries.title: Balloon rocket across the kitchen
entries.body: Me and Mom made a balloon rocket. You put a string across the room and a straw on the string and tape a balloon to the straw. When you let go of the balloon it zooms. The first time the tape came off. The second time it went all the way across the kitchen and hit the fridge. I wonder if a bigger balloon would go all the way to the living room. Ivy screamed because it was loud. When I grow up I want my own lab and it will have lots of string.
entries.favorite: The balloon zooming on the string
entries.highlight: Built a balloon rocket on a string with Mom that zoomed across the kitchen on the second try.

entries.title: Last ride to school before winter break
entries.body: Today was the last day of school before winter break. On the ride to school everybody was singing jingle bells really loud. Wes kept poking me in the arm the whole time. It was annoying but funny. I told everyone that a black hole could eat the whole school bus. Wes said it could not eat him because he is too fast. I said nothing is faster than light. He said he is.
entries.highlight: Rode to school with friends on the last day before winter break, sang with friends, and argued with Wes about black holes.

entries.title: Car ride to the science museum
entries.body: Today Hazel's family and my family drove to the science museum. In the car Hazel asked are we there yet like twenty times, and her little cousin copied her every time. At the museum there was a giant swinging ball on a rope and it knocked over little pegs one at a time. The man said it is because the Earth is spinning. I do not feel the Earth spinning. Hazel said she does not either. We bought astronaut ice cream.
entries.highlight: Drove to the science museum with Hazel's family and saw a giant pendulum that shows the Earth spinning.

entries.title: Reindeer food with Hazel
entries.body: Hazel came over in the morning on Christmas Eve. We did experiments. We made reindeer food with oats and sprinkles and we put it on the grass so the reindeer can find our house. Hazel said reindeer cannot really fly. I said maybe they have rocket boots. We said we are lab partners forever. Then she had to go home. I am so excited for tomorrow I think I will never fall asleep.
entries.highlight: Made reindeer food with Hazel on Christmas Eve and debated whether reindeer can fly.

entries.title: My very own telescope
entries.body: Today was Christmas! I got a real telescope! It is blue and it has three legs and a little eyepiece. I named it Big Blue. Dad said we should wait until tonight but I could not wait. So we tried it right away even though it was freezing. At first I only saw black. Then Dad pointed it at the moon and I saw craters, real craters. I wonder what made all those holes. Ivy said it was a tele-scoop. I also got a book about the planets and new pajamas.
entries.favorite: Seeing the craters on the moon
entries.highlight: Got a telescope for Christmas, named it Big Blue, and saw craters on the moon with Dad on the very first night.

entries.title: Arjun came to see Big Blue
entries.body: Arjun came over in the afternoon on Christmas to see my new telescope. It was still light outside so we could not see stars. Arjun looked through it at the neighbor's chimney. We made slime with his new slime kit and it was glow in the dark. Then some got on the carpet next to the old slime spot. Before he went home it got dark and he saw the moon. He said whoa. We said we are lab partners forever.
entries.favorite: Arjun saying whoa at the moon
entries.highlight: Showed his friend Arjun his new telescope on Christmas and they made glow-in-the-dark slime.

entries.title: The glow slime experiment
entries.body: Arjun came back today because we wanted to test the glow slime. We held it under the lamp for a long time and then we went in the closet and turned off the lights. It glowed green. The longer we held it under the light the more it glowed. I think the light goes inside it and then comes back out. Arjun said it is like a battery for light. That is a good idea. Mom said no slime on the carpet again.
entries.highlight: Tested glow-in-the-dark slime with Arjun in a dark closet and noticed more light made it glow longer.

entries.title: Salt crystals on a string
entries.body: Me and Mom did growing salt crystals. We mixed salt in hot water until no more would melt. Then we hung a string in the jar from a pencil. Mom said it takes days. I checked it like twenty times. Tonight there are tiny tiny crystals on the string and they look like sugar. I want to do it again but bigger, with a giant jar. I wonder if I could make a crystal as big as my fist.
entries.favorite: The tiny crystals on the string
entries.highlight: Started a salt crystal experiment with Mom and saw tiny crystals form on the string.

entries.title: Mars for New Year's Eve
entries.body: It was New Year's Eve and I got to stay up late. While we waited I drew a picture of Mars. It is red because of rust in the dirt. I put a rocket and an astronaut on it, and the astronaut is me. I made the astronaut wave. Mom hung it on the fridge next to Jupiter. Then at midnight we banged pots in the kitchen. Ivy was already asleep. My New Year thing is to do more science.
entries.highlight: Drew himself as an astronaut on Mars while staying up for New Year's Eve and resolved to do more science.

entries.title: Roly polies hiding under the log
entries.body: I looked for bugs again in the backyard with my magnifying glass. It was cold but sunny. In the grass there was nothing. Then I flipped the log by myself this time. There were five roly polies all squished together. I think they are huddling to stay warm like penguins. I wonder if they know each other. I put the log back gently so they do not freeze. I let them all stay. I think bugs hide under logs because it is warmer there.
entries.highlight: Found five roly polies huddled under a log in winter and guessed they were staying warm together.

entries.title: Felix pokes and black holes
entries.body: On the ride to school everybody was singing and talking. Felix was doing a robot voice for everything. Then I told everyone about black holes from my book. If you fall in a black hole you stretch out like spaghetti. It is called spaghettification. Everybody said ewww. Felix said he wants to be spaghetti. Mrs. Lopez who was driving said nobody is turning into spaghetti in her van.
entries.highlight: Explained spaghettification in black holes to his friends on the ride to school, who found it gross and hilarious.

entries.title: Arjun and the paper helicopter
entries.body: Arjun came over and we did experiments. We made paper helicopters from a video. You cut the paper and fold the wings and put a paper clip on the bottom. Then we dropped them off the stairs and they spun around and around. Mine was faster because it had two paper clips. Arjun's was slower but spinnier. We said we are lab partners forever again. I think it means we have to keep saying it.
entries.highlight: Made spinning paper helicopters with Arjun and noticed the one with more paper clips fell faster.

entries.title: Pizza and a wizard movie
entries.body: We had movie night on Sunday. We watched the second wizard movie and we had pizza. Mom made popcorn after. In the movie a potion changed colors. I asked Mom if that is real. She said some things change color when you mix them, like with red cabbage. I want to try that. Ivy fell asleep on the couch with popcorn in her hand. Dad carried her to bed.
entries.highlight: Had pizza and a wizard movie night, and Mom told him some real mixtures change color like potions.

entries.title: I found the Big Dipper by myself
entries.body: Dad and me went in the backyard with Big Blue to look at the stars. It was so cold my nose hurt. Dad said the Big Dipper looks like a pot with a handle. He did not point. He said try to find it. I looked and looked and then I saw it, seven stars like a pot. I wonder who decided it looks like a pot. I found it by myself. Dad gave me a high five with his gloves. It was so cold but worth it.
entries.favorite: Finding the Big Dipper all by myself
entries.highlight: Found the Big Dipper on his own for the first time while stargazing with Dad on a freezing night.

entries.title: Recess on Mars would be longer
entries.body: Today I thought about what school would be like on Mars. A day on Mars is a little longer than a day on Earth so recess would be longer. That is the best part. But you could not play outside without a space suit. And the dust storms would cover the whole playground. The lunch would be space food in packets. I think I would still go. Mrs. Patel would need a helmet too.
entries.highlight: Imagined what school would be like on Mars, from longer recess to dust storms and space suits.

entries.title: Ice cream in January
entries.body: We went to the ice cream shop with my whole family even though it was January and cold. Dad said we are crazy. I got mint chip again because it is the best. Ivy got vanilla with rainbow sprinkles and she did not drop it this time. She held it with two hands. There was nobody else in the shop. I think ice cream melts slower in winter. That is my idea. I want to test it.
entries.highlight: Went for ice cream with the family on a cold January night and wondered if ice cream melts slower in winter.

entries.title: Nadia and the slime fix
entries.body: Nadia came over and we did experiments again. We made slime but this time I put the tray down first because of the slime spot. We added blue food coloring and glitter. Nadia said the glitter is like stars in space. It was very stretchy and we stretched it as long as the kitchen table. Then it broke in the middle. Nadia said that is like a black hole stretching you.
entries.highlight: Made glittery space slime with Nadia on a tray to keep it off the carpet.

entries.title: Page one of Captain Crater
entries.body: I started making my own comic book. It is about a space scientist named Captain Crater. He has a lab on the moon with a big dome. Page one is done. On page one Captain Crater wakes up and eats moon muffins. Then an alarm goes off. I wonder what the alarm is for. I do not know yet. I will figure it out on page two. I used my good markers.
entries.favorite: Drawing the moon lab on page one
entries.highlight: Started a comic book about a space scientist named Captain Crater who has a lab on the moon.

entries.title: My science notebook
entries.body: Mom gave me a science notebook, just for me. It has a green cover and I wrote LUKE'S LAB NOTES on it. Mom said scientists write what they think will happen first, and that is called a prediction. Then we did balloon rockets again. I predicted the long balloon would go farther than the round one. I was right! It made a big mess because one popped and Ivy cried. I wrote everything down anyway.
entries.highlight: Got his first science notebook from Mom and wrote his first prediction, which turned out to be right.

entries.title: Jupiter has moons too
entries.body: I drew another picture of Jupiter but this time I put moons around it. My planet book says Jupiter has a lot of moons and one is called Io and it has volcanoes. I wonder if the lava on Io is hot like ours. I drew Io with lava coming out. I put a rocket flying by and an astronaut waving out the window. This one is better than the first one because I did the stripes curvy. Mom said I am getting good at curvy.
entries.highlight: Drew Jupiter again, this time with its moons, including the volcanic moon Io.

entries.title: Bug notebook page
entries.body: I did a bug hunt again and I brought my lab notebook. It was a little warmer today. I found three roly polies and one tiny spider in the corner of the shed. I drew them in my notebook. Roly polies have fourteen legs. I counted with the magnifying glass. My prediction was there would be more bugs when it is warmer and that was a little bit right. I let them all go after.
entries.highlight: Brought his science notebook on a bug hunt, counted fourteen legs on a roly poly, and let the bugs go.

entries.title: Watching a real rocket launch
entries.body: We watched a real rocket launch on the computer. The countdown was so exciting. Ten, nine, eight. Dad and me counted out loud. Then there was fire and smoke and the rocket went up so fast. The man on the video said it was going to the space station. I want to be an astronaut. I asked Dad how long it takes to get to space and he said like ten minutes. That is shorter than a car ride to Grandma's. I wonder if astronauts get carsick.
entries.highlight: Watched a live rocket launch online with Dad and was amazed it reaches space in about ten minutes.

entries.title: Captain Crater's alarm
entries.body: I worked on my comic book about Captain Crater. I figured out the alarm on page two. It is because a moon rock robot is stuck in a crater. Captain Crater has to fly his moon buggy to save him. I drew the moon buggy with six wheels and a flag. I think the moon has a lot of craters because space rocks hit it. That is how Captain Crater got his name.
entries.favorite: Thinking of the moon rock robot
entries.highlight: Wrote page two of his Captain Crater comic, where the hero rescues a robot stuck in a moon crater.

entries.title: The closet lab, no sisters allowed
entries.body: I turned my closet into a lab. I moved my shoes out and put in a little table and my goggles and my magnifying glass and the lab notebook. I made a sign that says LUKE'S LAB, ONLY SCIENTISTS. My little sister is not allowed in. Ivy cried because she wanted to come in. Mom said maybe Ivy can be a visitor sometimes. I said only if she does not touch anything. She touches everything.
entries.highlight: Turned his closet into a lab with a sign saying only scientists, which upset his little sister Ivy.

entries.title: Car ride to Hazel's party
entries.body: Today we drove to Hazel's birthday party at the trampoline park. Hazel rode in our car because her mom had to bring the cake. She held the cake box on her lap the whole way so it would not slide. When she opened it at the party, it looked like a rocket ship with candles for flames. I told her the science fair is in eleven days and she said she is doing plants. I am doing crystals. At the party I jumped so high I felt like there was less gravity.
entries.favorite: Hazel's cake looked like a rocket ship
entries.highlight: Rode with Hazel to her trampoline park birthday party and they talked about their science fair projects.

entries.title: Red cabbage potion
entries.body: Remember the potion that changed colors in the wizard movie? Tonight me and Mom made a real one. She boiled red cabbage and the water turned purple. Then I put in lemon juice and it turned pink. Then I put in baking soda and it turned blue green. Mom said the cabbage water is an indicator and it tells you if something is an acid. I said it is basically magic. Mom said it is chemistry.
entries.highlight: Made a color-changing red cabbage indicator with Mom, a real version of the wizard movie potion.

entries.title: Dad and the moon model
entries.body: Dad helped me make a model of the moon for my room. We used a foam ball and gray paint. Then I poked craters in it with a pencil eraser. Dad said the dark spots on the moon are called seas but there is no water in them. That is so weird. I wonder why they called them seas then. We hung it next to Earth on my solar system. Now Earth has a moon. Saturn's rings are still a little crooked from last time.
entries.highlight: Made a foam moon model with craters with Dad and added it to the solar system above his bed.

entries.title: Can I join the tag game?
entries.body: At recess some kids were playing tag. I wanted to play but I was kind of shy. Arjun said just ask. So I said can I join? And they said yes. Then I got tagged right away and I was it. I chased Wes for a long time. The game kept getting bigger and bigger because more kids came. By the end of recess I was so sweaty. Next time I will ask right away.
entries.highlight: Got up the courage to ask to join a recess tag game, which kept growing bigger.

entries.title: Practice volcano the night before
entries.body: The science fair is in two days and I am nervous. My crystals are not growing very big. So to feel better me and Mom made a baking soda volcano for fun. We used a lot of vinegar and red food coloring. It foamed up and went all over the counter and onto the floor. It made a big mess. Mom said the bubbles are a gas called carbon dioxide. I said carbon dioxin. She said almost. I want to do it again but bigger.
entries.favorite: The volcano going all over the counter
entries.highlight: Made a messy practice volcano with Mom to calm his nerves two days before the science fair.

entries.title: Science fair and my honorable mention
entries.body: Science fair today. My project was growing salt crystals. My prediction was they would get as big as marbles. But they only got tiny, like sand. I almost cried when I set it up. A judge with glasses asked me why I think they stayed small. I said maybe I did not put enough salt. She said that is a great scientist answer. I got an honorable mention ribbon. It is green. Hazel got a blue ribbon for her plants. Mrs. Patel said a failed experiment still teaches you something.
entries.favorite: Getting a ribbon even though it did not work
entries.highlight: Was nervous at his first science fair when his crystals stayed tiny, but explained why to a judge and earned an honorable mention.

entries.title: Celebration ice cream
entries.body: After the science fair we went to the ice cream shop with my whole family to celebrate. I got mint chip in a cup. Ivy dropped hers again, the whole scoop, and I shared mine with her. Dad asked what honorable mention means and I said it means you did not win but it was still good. He said it means people noticed how hard you worked. I put my green ribbon on my lab door.
entries.highlight: Celebrated his science fair honorable mention with family ice cream and hung the ribbon on his lab.

entries.title: Lab upgrades and a visitor pass
entries.body: I worked on my closet lab. I put up my green ribbon and I put my test tubes from the kit in a cup. I made a shelf out of a shoe box for the notebook. My little sister is still not allowed in. Only scientists. But I made her a visitor pass out of paper so she can stand at the door and watch. She wore it around her neck all day. Mom said that was really kind.
entries.highlight: Upgraded his closet lab and made Ivy a paper visitor pass so she could watch from the door.

entries.title: The third wizard movie
entries.body: We watched the third wizard movie tonight. There was a part with a time machine necklace and I asked Dad if time travel is real. He said scientists think about it but nobody has done it. I think if I could time travel I would go to the science fair again and use more salt. Mom made popcorn and I made a potion from orange juice and fizzy water. It fizzed. I want to make potions for real still.
entries.highlight: Watched another wizard movie and said he would time travel back to the science fair to use more salt.

entries.title: Slime with more borax solution
entries.body: Me and Mom made slime again but I made it a real experiment. I made three cups. One had a little contact solution, one had medium, and one had a lot. I wrote a prediction in my notebook that the most one would be the best. But it was hard like rubber and it snapped. The medium one was the best. So my prediction was wrong. That is okay. I learned the middle amount is just right. I want to do it again but bigger.
entries.highlight: Tested three slime recipes, found his prediction was wrong, and learned the medium amount worked best.

entries.title: Captain Crater gets a sidekick
entries.body: I worked on my Captain Crater comic book. Page three is done. Captain Crater saved the moon rock robot and now the robot is his sidekick. The robot is named Bolts. I also drew a moon dog with a space helmet but I am not sure if he goes in the story. Mom said every comic needs a dog. Bolts says beep boop when he talks. I think Bolts is my favorite character.
entries.highlight: Finished page three of his comic, adding a robot sidekick named Bolts.

entries.title: Lemon battery round two
entries.body: The lemon battery did not work last time because the light did not turn on. Dad said one lemon is not enough. So me and Mom went to the store for more lemons. This time my list said eight lemons and a tiny light bulb. The lady at the store asked why so many lemons. I said for electricity. She said she hopes it is a bright idea. Mom laughed at that.
entries.favorite: The lady asking about all the lemons
entries.highlight: Went back to the store with Mom for more lemons after his first lemon battery could not light a bulb.

entries.title: Reading about Amelia Earhart
entries.body: Today in reading we learned about Amelia Earhart. She was a pilot a long time ago and she flew across the whole ocean by herself. I raised my hand two times. The first time I asked how she found her way. Mrs. Patel said with maps and a compass. The second time I asked if she was scared. Hazel sat next to me at lunch and we talked about if we would fly across the ocean. Hazel said yes. I said maybe. I wonder if I would be brave enough.
entries.highlight: Learned about Amelia Earhart in reading class, asked two questions, and talked about flying with Hazel at lunch.

entries.title: Bolts in trouble on page four
entries.body: Page four of my comic is done. There is a meteor shower on the moon and Bolts gets hit and his arm falls off. Captain Crater has to fix him in the moon lab with a wrench. I drew the meteors with orange lines behind them. Fun fact, meteors are just space rocks burning up. On the moon there is no air so they do not burn. They just hit. That is why there are so many craters.
entries.highlight: Drew page four of his comic and explained that the moon has craters because meteors do not burn up without air.

entries.title: Fixing Saturn's rings
entries.body: Tonight Dad helped me fix the solar system model. Saturn's rings were the hardest again. They were crooked since November. We took Saturn down and Dad cut new rings out of a plastic lid. Now they are clear like ice. My planet book says Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock so that makes sense. I hung it back up. Now it is perfect. Dad said finally.
entries.highlight: Fixed Saturn's crooked rings on the solar system model with Dad using a clear plastic lid.

entries.title: Nadia's pokes and the planets song
entries.body: On the ride to school everybody was singing and talking. We sang the planets song from music class. Every time we got to Uranus, Nadia giggled, and then everybody laughed every time. Then I told everyone that Uranus spins on its side like a rolling ball. Nobody believed me. Nadia said prove it. I said I will bring my planet book tomorrow and I did write it on my hand so I remember.
entries.highlight: Sang the planets song on the ride to school and promised Nadia he would prove Uranus spins on its side.

entries.title: The first green beetle of spring
entries.body: I looked at bugs with my magnifying glass in the backyard. It was finally warmer. I found a beetle with shiny green wings on the flowers. It looked like metal. I wonder if it is shiny so birds think it is not food. It walked on my finger and it tickled. I drew it in my science notebook and wrote the date. Last time in January I only found roly polies. My guess was the bugs come back when it is warm and that is right. I let them all go after.
entries.highlight: Found the first shiny green beetle of spring and noted in his notebook that bugs return when it warms up.

entries.title: Captain Crater page five
entries.body: Later on Saturday I did page five of the comic. Captain Crater gives Bolts a new arm and it has a claw now. Now Bolts can pick up moon rocks. Then Bolts says beep boop thank you. I did a big THE END but then I erased it because it is not the end. I want there to be an alien next. I am going to ask Arjun what the alien should look like because he is good at aliens.
entries.highlight: Drew page five of his comic, giving the robot a claw arm, and decided the story needs an alien next.

entries.title: The moon with a flag
entries.body: I drew a picture of the moon. I put a rocket and an astronaut on it and a flag. I also drew footprints. Dad said the real footprints from the astronauts are still on the moon because there is no wind to blow them away. That is so cool. They will be there forever probably. I drew my own footprints next to theirs. Someday they will be there for real.
entries.highlight: Drew astronauts and footprints on the moon after learning the real footprints are still there.

entries.title: A satellite moving across the sky
entries.body: Dad and me looked at the stars from the backyard. It was so cold but worth it. I saw a satellite moving. It looked like a star but it was moving slowly across the sky in a straight line. Dad said satellites do not have their own light. The sun shines on them. I wonder how many satellites there are. Dad said thousands. I said hi to it. It did not say hi back.
entries.highlight: Spotted a satellite crossing the night sky with Dad and learned satellites shine with reflected sunlight.

entries.title: Balloon rocket races
entries.body: Me and Mom had a balloon rocket race. I put two strings across the living room. My prediction was a bigger balloon goes farther. We blew mine up huge and Mom's small. Mine went all the way and Mom's stopped in the middle. Then Ivy let go of a balloon and it flew around the room making a farting noise. It made a big mess with the tape everywhere. My prediction was right this time.
entries.highlight: Raced balloon rockets with Mom and confirmed his prediction that a bigger balloon travels farther.

entries.title: Dad and me build a rocket model
entries.body: In the afternoon Dad and me started a model rocket out of a paper towel tube. It does not fly but it looks real. We put three fins on the bottom and a pointy cone on top. Dad said the fins keep a real rocket straight. I painted it white and wrote USA on the side and LUKE on the other side. I put it on my shelf next to my green ribbon.
entries.highlight: Built a paper towel tube model rocket with Dad and learned fins keep rockets flying straight.

entries.title: Tidy-Bot the room cleaning robot
entries.body: I designed a robot that cleans my room. Its name is Tidy-Bot. It has arms like a crane to pick up toys and a sock grabber for dirty socks. It would also make my bed in the morning. I drew it in my notebook with arrows. Mom said Tidy-Bot sounds great, but until it is built I still have to clean my room. That is not fair. I need to build it fast.
entries.highlight: Designed Tidy-Bot, a crane-armed robot to clean his room, and was told he still has to clean until it is built.

entries.title: The space food machine idea
entries.body: I invented a machine that makes space food. You put in the regular food at the top and there is a piston that pushes it through a tube. Then it comes out in a little packet for astronauts. Everybody would want one. I drew it with a big button that says GO. I asked Dad what a piston is really and he said it is a thing that pushes back and forth, like in a car engine. That is what I thought.
entries.favorite: The piston pushing the food out
entries.highlight: Invented a space food machine with a piston that pushes food through a tube into astronaut packets.

entries.title: The rainbow glass I shook
entries.body: I made a rainbow in a glass with sugar water and food coloring. Each color has a different amount of sugar. The heavy one goes on the bottom. Mom said that is called density. It made red, yellow, green, blue in layers. It was so pretty. Then I picked it up to show Dad and I shook it by accident and it all turned brown. I was mad. But Mom said now I know it has to stay still. I wonder if honey would make an even heavier layer.
entries.favorite: The colors staying in layers before I shook it
entries.highlight: Made a layered sugar water rainbow, learned about density, and accidentally shook it into brown.

entries.title: Pizza night and Pluto
entries.body: Sunday night we had pizza for dinner. Then I asked Dad why Pluto is not in my solar system model. He said Pluto is a dwarf planet now. I said that is mean to Pluto. So Dad helped me make a tiny Pluto from clay and we hung it way at the edge. Dad did a funny little Pluto voice saying I am still here. Ivy laughed so hard milk came out her nose.
entries.highlight: Added a tiny clay Pluto to his solar system model with Dad after learning it is a dwarf planet.

entries.title: Nadia and the fizzy surprise
entries.body: Nadia came over after school. It was April Fools Day. We did an experiment where you put baking soda under the paper and then pour vinegar. Nadia did not know and it fizzed and she screamed. Then she laughed. Then she taught me a trick with a penny and a magnet. We said we are lab partners forever. Then we wrote a lab rule together. Rule one, always wear goggles. We both signed it like a real contract.
entries.highlight: Played an April Fools fizz trick on Nadia, then they wrote and signed their first official lab rule together.

entries.title: The rocket boosters landed
entries.body: We watched another real rocket launch on the computer. The countdown was so exciting. But this time after it went up, part of the rocket came back down and landed standing up on a boat. Dad said it is called a booster and they reuse it. That is like recycling a rocket. I did not know rockets could land. I want to be an astronaut, or maybe the person who lands the boosters.
entries.highlight: Watched a rocket launch with Dad and was amazed to see the booster land upright on a boat.

entries.title: Wizard movie and Ivy's wand
entries.body: We watched a wizard movie at home on Thursday because there was no school tomorrow. Mom made popcorn. Ivy had a stick from the yard as a wand and kept saying the spells wrong. She said wingardium lemonade. I laughed so hard. I want to make potions for real still, but now I know they are called experiments. I told Ivy that. She said hers is a spell.
entries.highlight: Watched a wizard movie with the family and laughed when Ivy mixed up a spell with her stick wand.

entries.title: Explaining black holes again
entries.body: On the ride to school everybody was singing and talking. Then I told everyone about black holes again because I finished the whole library book. A black hole is a star that died and squished down really small. Wes said that is sad. Then he said I am a black hole expert. Felix asked what is inside a black hole and I said nobody knows. That made everybody quiet. Then we sang again.
entries.favorite: Wes saying I am a black hole expert
entries.highlight: Shared what he learned from finishing his black hole book on the ride to school, and Wes called him a black hole expert.

entries.title: A spring night and a red dot
entries.body: After dinner Dad and me looked at the stars from the backyard. It was not so cold this time, I only needed a sweatshirt. I saw a satellite moving again. Then I found the Big Dipper fast because I know it now. Then Dad showed me a star that looked a little red. He said that is Mars. I saw Mars with my own eyes! I looked at it in Big Blue and it was a small orange dot. I wonder if Mars looks red up close too.
entries.favorite: Finding a red dot that was Mars
entries.highlight: Found the Big Dipper quickly and saw Mars as a red dot through his telescope with Dad.

entries.title: Shopping for glow slime stuff
entries.body: I needed ingredients for slime so me and Mom went to the store after school. This time I want to make magnetic slime. You need iron powder but the store did not have it. So we got glue and glitter and another bottle of contact solution. The lady at the store asked what I was making and I said a science experiment. She said she used to love science. I think everybody likes science secretly.
entries.favorite: The lady asking what I was making
entries.highlight: Shopped for slime supplies with Mom, couldn't find iron powder for magnetic slime, and chatted with the cashier about science.

entries.title: If school was on Saturn
entries.body: Tonight before bed I thought about what school would be like on Saturn. But Saturn is made of gas so there is no ground. The school would have to float. A floating kid would say can I join and float over to the tag game. Recess would be in the rings. You could slide on the ice chunks. I think it would be cold. Mrs. Patel would float too and she would have to hold the papers down.
entries.highlight: Imagined a floating school on gassy Saturn with recess on the icy rings.

entries.title: Car ride to the kite festival
entries.body: On Sunday Arjun came with us to the kite festival at the park. In the car Arjun held his kite on his lap like a baby. I told everyone about black holes but Arjun said not again. So I talked about wind instead. At the park Arjun's kite went so high it looked like a dot. Mine got stuck in a tree. Dad got it down with a long stick. I think more wind higher up is why it went so high.
entries.highlight: Went to a kite festival with Arjun, got his kite stuck in a tree, and wondered why there is more wind higher up.

entries.title: Straws for a bigger balloon rocket
entries.body: After the kites me and Mom went to the store to get supplies for a giant balloon rocket. My list said long string, the big party balloons, bendy straws, and tape. I want my balloon rocket to go all the way down the hallway and into the kitchen. Mom said maybe the backyard. I picked the longest string they had. It is fifty feet. That is so long.
entries.highlight: Shopped with Mom for supplies for a giant fifty-foot balloon rocket.

entries.title: A planet book that tells you how far
entries.body: It was library day and I got a book about the planets. It has a chart of how far each planet is from the sun. Neptune is so far it takes the sunlight four hours to get there. I read half of it already. The librarian said I can renew it if I need more time. I asked if I can renew it forever. She said no. I will read it to Ivy at bedtime.
entries.highlight: Checked out a planet book that shows distances from the sun and read half of it on the first day.

entries.title: Jupiter and a rocket with a window
entries.body: I drew a picture of Jupiter again. It is my third Jupiter. Mom hung it on the fridge and took down the first one from November. I put a rocket and an astronaut on it. The rocket has a round window and you can see the astronaut looking out. I can tell my drawings are getting better. The first Jupiter looks like a pumpkin. This one looks like a real planet.
entries.highlight: Drew his third Jupiter and noticed how much better it looked than his first one from November.

entries.title: The alien named Blip
entries.body: I worked on my comic book. Page six has an alien. Arjun helped me think of it. The alien is named Blip and it is green and it has three eyes and it lives inside a crater. At first Captain Crater thinks Blip is bad, but Blip just wants to be friends. He says can I join? That is my favorite part. Now Captain Crater, Bolts, and Blip are a team.
entries.highlight: Added a friendly three-eyed alien named Blip to his comic, with ideas from his friend Arjun.

entries.title: The beetle that played dead
entries.body: I looked at bugs with my magnifying glass in the backyard after school. I found a beetle with shiny green wings again, maybe the same one. When I touched it, it stopped moving and turned on its back. I thought I hurt it. But then after like a minute it flipped over and walked away. Mom said some bugs play dead to trick animals that want to eat them. I wonder how it knows when it is safe to get up. I wrote that in my science notebook. I let them all go after.
entries.highlight: Watched a beetle play dead and learned that some bugs do that to trick predators.

entries.title: Learning to tell time with clocks
entries.body: Today in math we learned something new. We learned how to tell time on the clocks with hands. Quarter past and half past were tricky. I raised my hand two times. Mrs. Patel asked what quarter past three is and I said three fifteen. I got it right. I asked why clocks go to twelve and not ten. She said that is a great question and she would find out. She did not know.
entries.highlight: Learned to tell time on analog clocks in math and asked why clocks go to twelve.

entries.title: Felix and the paper bridge
entries.body: Felix came over after school and we did experiments. We made a bridge out of paper between two books. Flat it held two pennies. Then we folded the paper like a fan and it held twenty pennies! Felix said it is like the ridges make it strong. I wrote it in my notebook. We said we are lab partners forever. Felix said he is the engineer and I am the scientist. That works.
entries.highlight: Built a folded paper bridge with Felix that held twenty pennies and wrote the result in his notebook.

entries.title: Painting with salt in art
entries.body: Today in art we learned something new. We painted with watercolors and then sprinkled salt on the wet paint. It was hard at first because I put too much water and it got all puddly. But then I got it. The salt soaked up the color and made little star shapes. I made a night sky. I told Mrs. Patel it is like my crystals. She said I see science everywhere.
entries.highlight: Learned a watercolor salt technique in art and made a starry night sky painting.

entries.title: Building the space food machine
entries.body: I built the space food machine for real, out of cardboard. Dad gave me a big box. I made a conveyor belt with a paper towel roll and a long strip of paper that you turn with a handle. Then the piston is a toilet paper tube that slides into a bigger tube and pushes the food out. I tested it with a grape. The grape came out squished. It works! Kind of. It is my first real invention.
entries.highlight: Built his first real invention, a cardboard space food machine with a working hand-cranked conveyor belt and piston.

entries.title: Felix tests the space food machine
entries.body: Felix came over to test my space food machine. We put in crackers this time. The conveyor belt worked but the piston squished the cracker into crumbs. Felix ate the crumbs anyway and said tastes like space. Then I told him that in space crumbs are bad because they float into your eyes. Felix said then we need a crumb catcher. That is a good idea. We said we are lab partners forever.
entries.highlight: Tested his space food machine with Felix, who suggested adding a crumb catcher.

entries.title: Oobleck is solid and liquid
entries.body: After Felix went home me and Mom made oobleck. It is cornstarch and water. When you push it slow your finger goes in like it is water. When you punch it fast it is hard like a rock. Mom said it is a non-Newton fluid. I said a non-newt fluid. She said close, Newtonian. That is a hard word. It made a big mess on the table. I want to do it again but bigger, like a whole pool you can run on.
entries.highlight: Made oobleck with Mom and was amazed that it acts like a liquid when pushed slowly and a solid when punched.

entries.title: Supplies for elephant toothpaste
entries.body: I needed ingredients for elephant toothpaste so me and Mom went to the store on Sunday. I wrote the list on a sticky note. Dish soap, yeast, food coloring, a tall bottle, and hydrogen peroxide. Mom said the peroxide is a grown-up only part and she will pour it. I said okay but I get to do the yeast. The man at the checkout asked if we have an elephant. I said no, a little sister.
entries.favorite: Mom saying the peroxide is grown-up only
entries.highlight: Shopped for elephant toothpaste supplies with Mom, who said she would handle the hydrogen peroxide.

entries.title: I asked to join right away
entries.body: At recess there was a tag game again. Last time I was shy but this time I asked can I join right away. They said sure. It was freeze tag. If you get tagged you have to freeze like a statue. I froze like an astronaut floating. Nadia unfroze me by going under my legs. Then I was it and I tagged Wes by the slide. Wes said he let me. He did not let me.
entries.highlight: Asked to join a recess freeze tag game right away this time and tagged Wes by the slide.

entries.title: Moon phases with a lamp
entries.body: Dad and me made a model of the moon phases. He took the shade off a lamp and that was the sun. I held a ball on a stick, that was the moon, and my head was Earth. When I turned around slowly the light on the ball changed from full to half to a skinny crescent. That is why the moon looks different every night! It is not getting eaten. I used to think that. Now I know. Now I wonder what Earth looks like from the moon.
entries.favorite: Seeing the half moon on the ball
entries.highlight: Used a lamp and a ball with Dad to understand why the moon has phases.

entries.title: A book about astronaut food
entries.body: It was library day and I got a book about what astronauts eat. Astronauts drink juice out of pouches with straws. They eat shrimp cocktail sometimes. That is weird. And they have to put food on velcro so it does not float away. I read half of it already. This is good research for my space food machine. The librarian said I am the space food expert now. I will tell Felix.
entries.favorite: Learning that astronauts velcro their food
entries.highlight: Checked out a book about astronaut food as research for his space food machine.

entries.title: Salt crystals with way more salt
entries.body: Remember at the science fair my crystals were tiny? I tried again with Mom. This time I put in salt until it would not melt anymore and there was salt at the bottom. Mom said that is called saturated. Then we put the jar on the windowsill and waited five days. Today they are as big as peas! The judge was right. It was the salt. A failed experiment still teaches you something, like Mrs. Patel said.
entries.favorite: The crystals being as big as peas
entries.highlight: Retried his science fair salt crystals with a saturated solution and grew pea-sized crystals.

entries.title: The ant highway
entries.body: I looked at bugs with my magnifying glass in the backyard. I found an ant highway going from the sidewalk to the grass. I put a cracker crumb down to see what they would do. At first one ant found it. Then like twenty came. They carried it together like a team. I wonder how they tell each other. Dad said ants leave a smell trail. I let them keep the cracker.
entries.highlight: Watched an ant trail team up to carry a cracker crumb and learned ants leave scent trails.

entries.title: Planet card for Ivy's birthday
entries.body: Ivy is turning four tomorrow so I made her a birthday card. I drew all the planets and on each one I drew Ivy. Ivy on Mars, Ivy on Saturn, Ivy on the moon. On the inside I wrote happy birthday lab visitor. I know she will like it because she likes when I draw her. Mom said it is very thoughtful. I hid it under my pillow so she does not see it until tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Drew a planet birthday card for Ivy's fourth birthday with her pictured on every planet.

entries.title: My first chapter book all by myself
entries.body: Today in reading we learned about chapter books and I finished my first one all by myself. It is about a magic tree house that takes kids to space. They go to the moon and meet an astronaut. I raised my hand two times to tell about it. Mrs. Patel said I can do a book report. Hazel sat next to me at lunch and said she wants to read it next. I said it is so good.
entries.highlight: Finished his first chapter book independently, a space adventure, and was invited to do a book report.

entries.title: Bean seeds and paper towels
entries.body: I needed ingredients for a plant experiment so me and Mom went to the garden store. Hazel did plants at the science fair and got a blue ribbon so now I want to try. My list was short. Bean seeds, paper towels, plastic baggies. My prediction is the bean in the sunny window will grow faster than the bean in the dark closet. The lady at the garden store said beans are good for beginners.
entries.highlight: Shopped for bean seeds with Mom to test whether light helps plants grow, inspired by Hazel's project.

entries.title: Ivy is my lab assistant now
entries.body: Ivy is four now so I said she can come in my lab, but only as my lab assistant. She has to wear goggles. The goggles were too big and fell down her nose. I showed her how to mix baking soda and vinegar in a cup. She poured it and it fizzed and she screamed happy. Then she wanted to do it ten more times. It was kind of fun teaching her. I made her a name tag that says LAB ASSISTANT.
entries.highlight: Let Ivy into his closet lab for the first time as his official lab assistant and taught her a fizzing experiment.

entries.title: The rainbow glass, no shaking
entries.body: I made the rainbow in a glass again. Last time I shook it by accident and it turned brown. This time I used a dropper from my kit and put each color in slow, down the side of the glass. I did not touch it after. It stayed in layers. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple. I took a picture with Mom's phone and printed it for my notebook. I learned to be patient. Patience is hard.
entries.highlight: Made a perfect layered rainbow in a glass by adding colors slowly with a dropper, learning patience from his earlier mistake.

entries.title: The launch that got scrubbed
entries.body: We were going to watch a real rocket launch on the computer. The countdown got to five minutes and then they stopped it. They said there was too much wind up high. Dad said that is called a scrub. I was so mad because I waited all day. Dad said it is better to wait than to have the rocket go the wrong way. I guess that makes sense. They will try again on another day. I wonder how they measure the wind way up high.
entries.highlight: Waited for a rocket launch that got scrubbed for high winds and learned why safety comes first.

entries.title: A rainbow on the ceiling
entries.body: I made a different kind of rainbow today. I put a glass of water on the window in the sun and a rainbow came out on the ceiling. Mom said the water bends the light and splits it into colors. That is called refraction. I made Ivy look and she tried to touch it but it is just light. Then a cloud came and the rainbow was gone. I want to make one in my lab but there is no window.
entries.highlight: Made a rainbow appear on the ceiling with a glass of water in the sun and learned the word refraction.

entries.title: Ivy wants to be in the comic
entries.body: I worked on my Captain Crater comic. Page seven is done. Ivy asked if she can be in it. At first I said no, it is a space scientist comic. Then I thought maybe Captain Crater needs a lab assistant. So I drew a little girl with big goggles named Ivy Star. Ivy said her superpower is she can make things fizz. That is actually kind of funny. Now the team has four people.
entries.highlight: Added his little sister to his comic as a lab assistant named Ivy Star with a fizzing superpower.

entries.title: A cover for my comic
entries.body: I drew the cover for my comic book. It says CAPTAIN CRATER AND THE MOON LAB in bubble letters. Under it I drew the whole team. Captain Crater, Bolts the robot, Blip the alien, and Ivy Star. Mom said it looks like a real comic from the store. I am going to show Mrs. Patel tomorrow if she has time. I still have to finish the end. I do not know how it ends. I wonder how real comic artists figure out their endings.
entries.highlight: Drew a cover for his comic book showing the whole team, though he is still figuring out the ending.

entries.title: The ice cream melting race
entries.body: We went to the ice cream shop with my whole family. In January I wondered if ice cream melts slower in winter. Today it was hot so I tested it a little. I put a spoonful on the sidewalk in the sun and one in the shade. The sun one melted in like two minutes. The shade one took way longer. So yes, heat makes it melt faster. Mint chip is still the best.
entries.favorite: The sun spoonful melting in two minutes
entries.highlight: Tested his winter question about ice cream melting by putting scoops in the sun and shade at the ice cream shop.

entries.title: Ladybugs on the rose bush
entries.body: I looked at bugs with my magnifying glass in the backyard after school. I found four ladybugs on Mom's rose bush. Mom said they are good bugs because they eat the aphids that hurt the roses. I counted their spots. One had seven, one had two, and two had none. I did not know ladybugs could have no spots. I wonder if the spots tell how old they are. I drew them in my science notebook. I let them all go after, back on the roses.
entries.highlight: Found four ladybugs on the rose bush, counted their spots, and learned they help protect the plants.

entries.title: Summer plans on the ride to school
entries.body: On the ride to school everybody was singing and talking about summer. There are only two more days of school. Wes is going to the beach. Nadia is going to her grandma's. I said I am doing science camp. Felix said science camp sounds like school. I said no, it is fun school. Wes kept poking me. Annoying but funny. Then I told everyone the sun is a star. They already knew.
entries.highlight: Talked about summer plans on the ride to school, including his upcoming science camp, two days before school ended.

entries.title: Watching a launch in class
entries.body: We watched a real rocket launch on the computer at school. Mrs. Patel put it on the big screen because she knew I love rockets. The whole class counted down together. Ten, nine, eight. It went up and everybody cheered. It was not scrubbed this time. I told the class that part of it will land on a boat. Mrs. Patel let me explain the booster. I felt like a real scientist.
entries.highlight: Watched a rocket launch with his whole class and got to explain how boosters land.

entries.title: The best question asker in second grade
entries.body: Last day of school today. Second grade is done! We had a little party and Mrs. Patel gave everybody a paper award. Mine said Best Question Asker. She said I asked more questions than anybody she ever had. I asked her one more. I said did you find out why clocks go to twelve? She laughed and said it is because of the ancient Egyptians. I am going to miss her. Now it is summer.
entries.favorite: Mrs. Patel calling me the best question asker
entries.highlight: Finished second grade and Mrs. Patel gave him the Best Question Asker award.

entries.title: The lemon battery flickered
entries.body: Me and Mom did the lemon battery again. This time we used four lemons and connected them with wires in a line. Each lemon had a zinc screw and a copper piece. My prediction was a big bright light. But when we put the tiny red light on, it only flickered a little bit, really dim. But it was on! The lemons made electricity! Mom said maybe more lemons would be brighter. I want to do it again but bigger.
entries.highlight: Connected four lemons into a battery with Mom and got a tiny red light to flicker on.

entries.title: My summer lab list
entries.body: Summer is here so I made a list in my lab notebook of all the experiments I want to do this summer. Number one is make craters by dropping rocks in flour. Number two is the giant balloon rocket. Number three is magnet stuff. Number four is make Tidy-Bot real. Ivy wanted to put something on the list so I wrote number five, Ivy's fizz. My lab is getting hot in the closet in summer though.
entries.favorite: Writing number one, make a crater
entries.highlight: Wrote a summer science to-do list in his notebook, including an item for Ivy.

entries.title: A hose rainbow in the yard
entries.body: Remember the rainbow on the ceiling from the glass of water? Today I made one outside. I stood with my back to the sun and sprayed the hose up high in a mist. A rainbow came out in the water. Ivy ran through it and got soaked and I did too. It is the same thing, the water drops bend the light. That is how real rainbows happen after it rains. Refraction is my new favorite word.
entries.highlight: Made a rainbow with the garden hose mist and connected it to how real rainbows form after rain.

entries.title: A crystal for Father's Day
entries.body: Today was Father's Day. I grew a special salt crystal for Dad. I made a saturated solution like last time and hung one string so all the salt grew on just one string. It took a week. I put it in a little box with a card that says to the best stargazing dad. He said it is the coolest present he ever got. He put it on his desk at work. I think he really liked it.
entries.highlight: Grew a salt crystal as a Father's Day gift for Dad, who put it on his desk.

entries.title: Tidy-Bot version two with Dad
entries.body: Tonight Dad and me redesigned Tidy-Bot together. The first one had crane arms but Dad asked how does it move around? I forgot about that. So version two has wheels like a vacuum robot and a basket on top for toys. It has a sensor so it does not crash into my bed. I drew it in my notebook and wrote version 2 on top. It would also make my bed. Dad said that part is the hardest.
entries.highlight: Redesigned his room-cleaning robot Tidy-Bot with Dad, adding wheels and a sensor.

entries.title: A crumb catcher for the machine
entries.body: I added a crumb catcher to my space food machine. It was Felix's idea. It is a plastic cup taped under the piston. Now when the piston squishes the crackers, the crumbs fall in the cup instead of on the floor. I tested it with goldfish crackers. Most crumbs went in. In space they would float so I would need a lid. I am going to add a lid next. It is version two.
entries.highlight: Added a crumb catcher to his space food machine based on Felix's idea and tested it with crackers.

entries.title: Ice cream in a bag
entries.body: We did not go to the ice cream shop today. We made our own ice cream in a bag. You put milk and sugar in a little bag and then put it in a big bag with ice and salt and shake it. The salt makes the ice colder. My hands were freezing. After ten minutes it was ice cream for real. Ivy's bag leaked. I shared mine with her again. Every time, Ivy.
entries.favorite: Shaking the bag until it got cold
entries.highlight: Made homemade ice cream in a bag with salt and ice and once again shared with Ivy after her bag leaked.

entries.title: Counting firefly flashes
entries.body: After dinner I looked at bugs in the backyard but it was almost dark. There were fireflies everywhere! I caught one in my hands and it lit up between my fingers. Dad said they light up to talk to each other. I counted how long between flashes. Some were fast and some were slow. I wonder if the fast ones are boys and the slow ones are girls. I do not know yet. I let them all go after.
entries.highlight: Caught a firefly at dusk, timed the flashes, and made a guess about why they differ.

entries.title: Sun prints with Hazel
entries.body: Hazel came over and we did experiments. We made sun prints. It is special paper that turns white where you put stuff on it and blue where the sun hits it. Hazel used a fern leaf and it came out perfect. I used my toy rocket and it came out like a white rocket shape. We said we are lab partners forever. Hazel said she is coming to science camp too. That is the best news.
entries.highlight: Made sun prints with Hazel and found out she is coming to science camp too.

entries.title: Riding to science camp
entries.body: It was the first day of science camp so we shared a ride even though it is summer. Me and Hazel and Wes all rode together in Wes's mom's car. Everybody was singing and Wes's mom made us say our names and one science word before she started the car. At camp we made rockets out of film canisters and an antacid tablet and water. You snap the lid on and it pops up into the air. Mine went higher than the basketball hoop. Wes's popped on his shoe.
entries.highlight: Rode to the first day of science camp with Hazel and Wes and launched film canister rockets.

entries.title: Water bottle rockets with Hazel
entries.body: Hazel came over on Sunday and we did experiments outside because it was so hot. Dad helped us make a water bottle rocket. You fill the bottle a little with water and pump air into it with a bike pump. Then it shoots up. The first one only went a little because we put too much water. The second one went over the fence into the neighbor's yard. Hazel wrote it down in my notebook. We said lab partners forever. I think less water is better.
entries.favorite: Our rocket going over the fence
entries.highlight: Launched water bottle rockets with Hazel and Dad, discovering that less water made them fly farther.

entries.title: Moving my lab to the garage
entries.body: My closet lab got too hot in the summer. My goggles got all foggy. So Dad said I can have a corner of the garage for summer. There is a real workbench with a vise and a lamp. I moved my notebook and my test tubes and my green ribbon. I put the LUKE'S LAB sign on the wall. Ivy has her own stool now. I said she can be lab assistant if she does not touch the vise. It feels like a real lab now.
entries.highlight: Moved his lab from the hot closet to a corner of the garage with a real workbench and a stool for Ivy.

entries.title: Movie night about real astronauts
entries.body: We had movie night but this time we watched a movie about the real astronauts who went to the moon. It was old and some parts were black and white. They were so brave. The rocket was so big, way bigger than the ones we watch now. When they stepped on the moon everybody in the movie cheered. Ivy asked if I am going to the moon. I said yes, someday. She asked if she can come. I said if she is still my lab assistant.
entries.highlight: Watched a movie about the real moon landing with the family and promised Ivy she could come to the moon someday.

entries.title: A cicada shell on the tree
entries.body: I looked at bugs with my magnifying glass in the backyard. I found a cicada shell stuck on the tree. It is the skin they leave when they grow out of it, like taking off a jacket. It is crunchy and see-through and it still has legs. I wonder if it hurts to come out of your skin. Then I heard the real cicadas buzzing so loud. Dad said they are the loudest bugs. I put the shell in my lab on a shelf. It is my first specimen. I let the live ones stay in the tree.
entries.favorite: The cicada screaming in the tree
entries.highlight: Found a cicada shell and kept it as the first specimen in his lab.

entries.title: I saw Saturn's rings with my own eyes
entries.body: Dad woke me up really late last night, like eleven, and said come outside. He had Big Blue pointed at a bright dot. I looked in the eyepiece and it was Saturn with the rings! The real rings! It was tiny but it looked exactly like the pictures. It did not even look real. I wonder how something so far away can look so sharp. I made Dad look and then I looked again like ten times. I have been waiting since Christmas to see that. It was worth staying up so late.
entries.favorite: Seeing the rings in Big Blue
entries.highlight: Saw Saturn's rings through his telescope for the first time after waiting since Christmas.

entries.title: School on Jupiter would crush you
entries.body: Today I thought about what school would be like on Jupiter. But I know now that Jupiter does not have any ground. It is a gas giant so the school would fall into the clouds forever. Also the gravity is so strong you would feel super heavy. Walking to lunch would be like carrying three backpacks. And there is that red spot storm that is bigger than Earth. So school on Jupiter would be a bad idea. I think the moons would be better, like Europa.
entries.highlight: Reasoned that a school on Jupiter would not work because it has no ground and crushing gravity, and suggested its moon Europa instead.

entries.title: Soda and mints for a geyser
entries.body: I needed ingredients for a soda geyser so me and Mom went to the store. You need a two liter bottle of diet soda and a pack of mint candies. I made a list like a real scientist and I also wrote my prediction. I think it will go as high as the garage roof. Mom said we have to do it in the driveway, not the lab. The cashier said you are going to get sticky. I said that is the point.
entries.highlight: Shopped for diet soda and mints with Mom to try a soda geyser and predicted how high it would go.

entries.title: What do magnets stick to?
entries.body: I did a magnet test with Mom. I walked around the house with a big magnet and my notebook and wrote my prediction for each thing before I tried it. The fridge stuck. The spoon I thought would stick but it did not. Mom said it is stainless steel and some kinds are not magnetic. I wonder what is different inside that spoon. Pennies did not stick either. The paper clip stuck. I got six right and four wrong. The wrong ones were the most interesting because they surprised me.
entries.highlight: Tested household objects with a magnet after writing predictions and found the surprises most interesting.

entries.title: Tortillas for the space food machine
entries.body: Tonight I read more of my astronaut food book that I renewed again. Astronauts do not eat bread in space because the crumbs float around and can get in the machines. They eat tortillas instead. So I changed my space food machine plans. Now the piston will press food into a tortilla and roll it up on the conveyor belt like a burrito. No crumbs! The crumb catcher was a good idea but no crumbs is even better.
entries.highlight: Redesigned his space food machine to roll food into tortillas after learning astronauts avoid crumbly bread.

entries.title: My first time rafting
entries.body: We went rafting on the river in a big yellow raft with a guide named Hank. Me and Dad went and Mom and Ivy watched from the beach because Ivy is too little. I was really nervous. I held the rope on the side so tight my hands hurt. When we went over the first bumpy part the water splashed in my face and I screamed. But then I started laughing. Hank said the bumpy parts are called rapids and the water is going fast because the river gets narrow there. By the end I paddled a little. Dad said I was a natural. I think I was half scared and half having fun.
entries.favorite: Dad saying I was a natural
entries.highlight: Went rafting for the first time with Dad, started out nervous gripping the rope, and ended up paddling and laughing.

entries.title: Stuck on the ending of my comic
entries.body: I worked on my Captain Crater comic for a long time today. I have eight pages and a cover but I am stuck on the ending. I tried three endings. In one they find water on the moon. In one Blip goes home to his planet. In one the moon lab blows up, but that one is too sad. Mom said real writers get stuck too and sometimes they take a break. So I am taking a break. I drew Bolts doing a dance on the back of page eight while I think. Maybe Bolts should save the day at the end because he was the one who got saved at the beginning.
entries.favorite: Bolts saving the day in my idea
entries.highlight: Worked on his comic's ending, tried three versions, and decided to take a break like real writers do.

entries.title: Explaining potions to Ivy
entries.body: We watched the first wizard movie again because Ivy never saw it. She sat on my lap for the scary parts. When they made potions I explained to her that real potions are called chemical reactions. Like when we do baking soda and vinegar, that makes a gas. Or when the cabbage water changes color, that is because of acids. Ivy said so you are a wizard scientist. I said kind of. Mom made popcorn and Dad made it extra salty. Last year I just wanted to make potions. Now I actually know how some of them work, and that is even better.
entries.highlight: Watched a wizard movie with Ivy and explained that real potions are chemical reactions like the ones they do in his lab.

entries.title: Back to school ice cream
entries.body: We went back to school shopping and I got a new backpack with planets on it. Then we went to the ice cream shop with my whole family. I got mint chip, of course. Ivy got cotton candy flavor and she held it with two hands and did not drop it, not even one drip. She said look Luke, I did not drop it. I gave her a high five. Last November she dropped her whole scoop on the sidewalk and cried. She is getting bigger. Dad said I am getting bigger too because I am going to be in third grade. I hope Mr. Brooks likes space.
entries.highlight: Went for back to school ice cream with the family and cheered Ivy for holding her cone without dropping it.

entries.title: A launch in the dark
entries.body: We watched a real rocket launch on the computer but this time it was at night. When the engines turned on the whole sky lit up orange and you could see the clouds from underneath. It looked like a sunrise but going up. The countdown was so exciting. Dad said night launches happen because the rocket has to go when the space station is in the right spot. That is called a launch window. I like that word. It sounds like a window in a rocket but it actually means a time. I wonder if the astronauts can see the city lights on the way up. I want to see one in real life, not just on the computer.
entries.highlight: Watched a night rocket launch with Dad and learned what a launch window is.

entries.title: First day of third grade
entries.body: First day of school today. I am in third grade now and my teacher is Mr. Brooks. He is tall and he has a beard and he has a giant planet poster on the wall. He said we are going to learn about planets this year! I raised my hand and said I have a telescope and I saw Saturn's rings. He said no way, you have to tell the class about it someday. Arjun is in my class and so is Hazel. Wes is in the other class. My new backpack got a lot of compliments. I think third grade is going to be good.
entries.favorite: Mr. Brooks having a planet poster
entries.highlight: Started third grade with Mr. Brooks, who has a planet poster and announced a planets unit.

entries.title: Starting my moon journal
entries.body: Tonight I started a moon journal. It is a new notebook just for the moon. Every night that it is clear, I go out with Dad and look at the moon and draw exactly what it looks like and write the date and the time. Tonight there was no moon at all, Dad said it is a new moon. So I drew an empty circle with dots around it. My goal is to do a whole month and see if it matches the lamp and ball model we made in May. My prediction is it will get bigger every night until it is full. Dad said he will remind me.
entries.highlight: Started a moon journal to draw the moon every clear night and test his prediction about the phases.

entries.title: Labels for my specimen shelf
entries.body: I worked on my lab in the garage. I have a lot of stuff now so I made labels for everything. My specimen shelf has the cicada shell, a snail shell, a rock with sparkles, and the salt crystal I did not give Dad. Each label has the name, where I found it, and the date. Dad said real museums do it like that. Ivy wanted a label too so I made one that says IVY, LAB ASSISTANT, FOUND IN THE KITCHEN. She thought that was hilarious. I also taped my summer list up and checked off what I finished. I did three out of five.
entries.highlight: Labeled the specimens in his garage lab like a museum, and made a funny label for Ivy too.

entries.title: Making craters in flour
entries.body: Number one on my summer list was make craters, so me and Mom went to the store for flour and cocoa powder. You put flour in a pan and sprinkle cocoa on top. Then you drop rocks in from different heights. My hypothesis was that the higher you drop it, the bigger the crater. That was right. But I also found out the bigger rock made a bigger crater even from low down. And the cocoa sprayed out in lines like the rays on the moon craters! I compared it to my moon book and they look the same. Now I can cross off number one.
entries.highlight: Made craters by dropping rocks into flour and cocoa, confirmed his hypothesis about height, and noticed rays like real moon craters.

entries.title: Labor Day drive to the lake
entries.body: There was no school because it was Labor Day, so we drove to the lake with Arjun's family. In the car Arjun and I played I spy and I spied a satellite dish. At the lake Arjun showed me how to skip rocks. You have to find a flat one and throw it sideways. My first ten just went plunk. Then I got one to skip four times. I asked why flat rocks skip and Arjun's dad said the rock bounces off the water when it is going fast and flat. I think it is like the boosters landing, but backwards.
entries.highlight: Drove to the lake with Arjun's family on Labor Day and learned to skip a rock four times.

entries.title: Tidy-Bot version three
entries.body: At Arjun's house they have a real robot vacuum. It bumped into their dog and the dog barked at it. I watched how it works. It goes straight until it bumps something and then it turns. So I designed Tidy-Bot version three. It has bumpers like the vacuum, and the crane arm from version one, and the basket from version two. It sorts things too. Legos go in one bin, socks go in another. I wrote down the problem, which is that it has to know what a sock is. Dad said that is the hardest part of robots, teaching them to see things.
entries.favorite: Arjun's robot vacuum bumping the dog
entries.highlight: Designed a third version of his Tidy-Bot after studying how a robot vacuum navigates at Arjun's house.

entries.title: Rafting again and I paddled the whole time
entries.body: We went rafting on the river again before it gets cold. Last time I held the rope the whole time. This time I paddled the whole time, even in the rapids! The guide, it was Hank again, said paddle hard on the right side and I did. The raft turned and we went right through the bumpy part. Water got in my mouth and it tasted like a lake. Dad cheered so loud. Mom and Ivy waved from the beach and Ivy yelled go Luke go. I was still a little scared at the start but less scared than last time. I want to go again next summer.
entries.favorite: Going through the rapids without holding the rope
entries.highlight: Went rafting a second time and paddled through the rapids instead of holding on, feeling much less scared.

entries.title: Movie night before my birthday
entries.body: Tomorrow is my birthday so tonight I got to pick the movie. I picked the one about the robot who cleans up Earth. It is kind of like Tidy-Bot except it is a trash robot. He was alone for a long time and then he finds a friend robot. Mom cried a little and Dad pretended he did not. We ate popcorn and grapes. Before bed Ivy gave me my card early because she could not wait. It was a drawing of me with a telescope. She wrote L-U-K-E all by herself. The K was backwards but that is okay.
entries.favorite: Ivy giving me a card early
entries.highlight: Picked a robot movie for the night before his birthday and Ivy gave him a card she wrote herself.

entries.title: Eight years old and a Saturn cake
entries.body: It was my birthday! I am eight now. My cake looked like a planet. It was Saturn, with yellow frosting and the rings were made of candy melts. Mom made it and Dad helped with the rings, because Saturn's rings are always the hardest. I had a science party with Arjun and four other kids. We made slime and did a balloon rocket race and everybody got goggles to take home. For presents I got a moon map poster and a red flashlight for stargazing. Dad said red light does not mess up your night eyes. I want to try it tonight.
entries.favorite: The Saturn cake with candy rings
entries.highlight: Turned eight with a Saturn cake and a science party with Arjun, and got a moon map and red stargazing flashlight.

entries.title: School on Neptune would be windy
entries.body: Today I thought about what school would be like on Neptune. Neptune has the fastest wind in the whole solar system. My book says over a thousand miles an hour. That is faster than an airplane. So everybody's homework would blow away, and the teacher's hair, and maybe the teacher.
